turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about that zero on his phone in the middle of a class, so start with who decided it and whether anyone heard him first.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now the basis for it.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. A paste shows when the words landed in that file, not who wrote them or where. And none of this was put to Owen before you entered a mark.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Then he'll bring it. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet, not one word in front of his class. What are you proposing?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students misquote, Hale, and a seventeen-year-old paraphrasing from memory isn't fraud. Show me that it's not a garbled version of a real line.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll search it myself tonight. Fine, there's no such line. Say exactly what you're offering, in terms I can have in writing.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.

Forty minutes in a classroom with no book against a take-home essay with the play open beside him isn't a comparison, it's two different tasks. And you've now shown me three things without once saying what you want from him.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and to put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite. Tonight's email says it's private, not in front of his class, that its mark replaces the zero, that nothing goes on his record, and that the zero was entered before anyone called me. Until he writes it, the zero comes out of the online gradebook where he and everyone else can see it.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Put the date and who's supervising in that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed in today's meeting that the zero was entered before I was contacted, and that under procedure 4.4 Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite, not in front of his class, whose mark replaces the zero with nothing placed on his record. I still require the zero removed from the online gradebook until that rewrite is marked, and the date and supervisor of the rewrite confirmed. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4; she still wants your written confirmation tonight, the zero taken out of the gradebook until the rewrite is marked, and the date and supervisor named, and that is the fair outcome, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her paste defence by inviting Owen to bring any other draft file, because it was dated, tied to his own work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground; the closest was leaving her objection to the September in-class sample unanswered, which she noticed.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said the September sample was a different task, answer it with another take-home piece of Owen's own work, since the school procedure asks you to consider other samples of his writing.
